No tests, no comments, I know, but it might be useful.  I use the builder pattern to get around having too many arguments from all the headers you can pass in.  Feel free to pilfer from it if you'd like.
Alright, I refactored the code, but I have a few questions going forward.
Should we call the project "fcrepo-java-client" or something else?
Should I get the code to fcrepo-exts first, issue a non-snapshot release, then make a pull request to fcrepo-camel to use the client?
The project looks like this right now:

thanks for the code samples... while I intend to expand this library to be both a sleek stateless core, and one or more reasonably easy to use clients, this ticket is just a first pass where I'll a) create the new project, and b) move (essentially unaltered) the code from fcrepo-camel to an external project.
Let me know how we should proceed with this when you get a chance. (see above comments)
Once you are ready, pass along the PRs for review.
Note: An fcrepo-java-client:0.1.0 release was made and used in fcrepo-camel.
, is there a ticket or a plan to subsequently swap this fcrepo-java-client into migration-utils?
: After the extraction of the client code, Karaf is not able to install the fcrepo-camel module. I think this is due to the fcrepo-java-client does not have a OSGi bundle associated with it.

2.  The basic semantics of typical Fedora 4 requests
For a first pass, just extract the FcrepoClient (and dependencies) from fcrepo-camel and rig up an integration test framework.

comments.body:
Hey Michael Durbin, here's something I was playing with a while ago that I dredged up and put on github: https://github.com/daniel-dgi/islandora-fcrepo-client

It's what eventually led to https://github.com/Islandora-CLAW/chullo

No tests, no comments, I know, but it might be useful. I use the builder pattern to get around having too many arguments from all the headers you can pass in. Feel free to pilfer from it if you'd like.

Alright, I refactored the code, but I have a few questions going forward.

Should we call the project "fcrepo-java-client" or something else?

Should I get the code to fcrepo-exts first, issue a non-snapshot release, then make a pull request to fcrepo-camel to use the client?

The project looks like this right now: https://github.com/mikedurbin/fcrepo-java-client
The commit to camel: https://github.com/mikedurbin/fcrepo-camel/commit/bbc0af9e18d81d35ab6ce2c34411a387f6faf38d

Former user thanks for the code samples... while I intend to expand this library to be both a sleek stateless core, and one or more reasonably easy to use clients, this ticket is just a first pass where I'll a) create the new project, and b) move (essentially unaltered) the code from fcrepo-camel to an external project.
Let me know how we should proceed with this when you get a chance. (see above comments)

Michael Durbin, your plan sounds good:
1. New project with name: fcrepo-java-client
2. Extract from fcrepo-camel

Once you are ready, pass along the PRs for review.

Resolved with:
https://github.com/fcrepo4-exts/fcrepo-camel/commit/1695a1d51d3552ac4599c9c5f90b3bb1526db5be
and
https://github.com/fcrepo4-exts/fcrepo-java-client/commit/985600802b369a6d67c82b54716e196525c680f3

Note: An fcrepo-java-client:0.1.0 release was made and used in fcrepo-camel.
Michael Durbin, is there a ticket or a plan to subsequently swap this fcrepo-java-client into migration-utils?

Andrew Woods, Michael Durbin: After the extraction of the client code, Karaf is not able to install the fcrepo-camel module. I think this is due to the fcrepo-java-client does not have a OSGi bundle associated with it.
Mohamed Mohideen Abdul Rasheed I have created a ticket for this: https://jira.duraspace.org/browse/FCREPO-1858
Unknown, Great! Thanks.

Repost of Dec 6th question:
Michael Durbin, is there a ticket or a plan to subsequently swap this fcrepo-java-client into migration-utils?

renderedFields.description:
We need a shared java client library for Fedora 4. It will be a good start even if it just includes:

1. Best practices for HttpClient creation
2. The basic semantics of typical Fedora 4 requests

For a first pass, just extract the FcrepoClient (and dependencies) from fcrepo-camel and rig up an integration test framework.
